# ^TNX research brief, as of 2026-08-04

I only used information published on or before 2026-08-04. Many search results were dated later, and I ignored them.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the Yahoo Finance daily close of ^TNX for 2026-09-01. That date is a Tuesday and a normal trading day, since Labor Day 2026 falls on September 7. ^TNX is quoted in percent (for example, 4.70), and it can differ by a basis point or two from Treasury's official daily rate.
- 2026-08-04: I tried to open the Yahoo Finance ^TNX history page, but the proxy refused the connection. I could not read the latest ^TNX close directly from the resolution source.
- 2026-08-03: The 10-year rate from Treasury data, as shown on YCharts, was 4.70%. [YCharts](https://ycharts.com/indicators/10_year_treasury_rate)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened yet that settles the question. The yield sits about 70 basis points above the bottom of the 4.0 to 5.5 range and about 80 basis points below the top.
- 2026-07-31: The 10-year closed at 4.75% and the 2-year at 4.28%. [ETF Trends](https://www.etftrends.com/fixed-income-content-hub/treasury-yields-snapshot-july-31-2026/)
- 2026-08-03: Penn Mutual said the 10-year ended the prior week near 4.74%, its highest since January 2025. Yields opened lower on August 3 after oil fell overnight. [Penn Mutual AM](https://www.pennmutualam.com/market-insights/blogs/monday-morning-perspectives/2026-08-03-us-treasury-yields-setting-fresh-2026-highs)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-03: Long-term Treasury yields hit fresh 2026 highs last week. Oil is the main thing moving prices day to day. [Penn Mutual AM](https://www.pennmutualam.com/market-insights/blogs/monday-morning-perspectives/2026-08-03-us-treasury-yields-setting-fresh-2026-highs)
- Late July 2026: Front-month WTI oil futures fell 8.1% in one session, to $82.04. [Kiplinger](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/live/fed-meeting-updates-and-commentary-july-2026)
- 2026-07-29: The Fed held its rate range at 3.50% to 3.75% by a 9 to 3 vote. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all dissented in favor of a rate hike, the most dissents since 2016. After the meeting the 10-year rose more than 7 basis points to 4.677%, and the 30-year topped 5.2%, its highest since 2007. Markets priced roughly a 76% to 82% chance of a September hike. Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference was read as dovish on inflation. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-meeting-today-live-updates.html), [Fed statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/monetary20260729a1.pdf), [BingX](https://bingx.com/en/blog/article/july-2026-fomc-fed-rate-decision-and-how-it-affects-stocks-gold-bitcoin-price)
- 2026-07-21: The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget noted the 10-year had passed 4.6%. [CRFB](https://www.crfb.org/blogs/10-year-treasury-yield-eclipsed-46)
- 2026-07-02: A weak June jobs report lowered expectations of a Fed hike. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/02/us-treasury-yields-rise-as-investors-await-june-jobs-report.html)
- 2026-02-27: The 10-year was 3.96% the day before the Middle East war began. Higher oil prices since then have pushed inflation worries and yields up. [Kiplinger](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/live/fed-meeting-updates-and-commentary-july-2026)

## 4. Base rates
- Recent path: about 3.96% in late February, above 4.6% by July 21, and about 4.70% to 4.75% from July 31 to August 3. That is a rise of roughly 75 to 80 basis points in five months, with the trend up.
- Typical one-month change: from my general knowledge, not a source I fetched this session, the 10-year has historically moved with a standard deviation of roughly 20 to 30 basis points per month. Moves of more than 40 basis points in a month happen but are uncommon, and are more likely in volatile times like this one, with an oil shock and possible Fed hikes.
- Single-day moves of 7 to 10 basis points happened around the July FOMC meeting.

## 5. Other forecasts
- July 2026: A Wall Street Journal survey of economists forecast the 10-year at 4.4% at the end of 2026, below the current level. [CRE Daily](https://www.credaily.com/?p=223963)
- Kalshi runs daily and year-end 10-year yield contracts (for example, the [daily UST 10-year series](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxust10ad/ust-10-year-daily/kxust10ad-26aug05)). I could not find a Kalshi market for September 1, or any year-end prices dated on or before August 4.
- I found nothing on Polymarket or Manifold for this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before September 1
- 2026-08-05: ADP private payrolls report. 2026-08-07: the July jobs report.
- Around 2026-08-12 and 08-13: July CPI and PPI inflation data.
- 2026-08-19: Minutes of the July FOMC meeting. The three dissents make any hawkish wording important.
- Around August 20 to 22: Warsh's Jackson Hole speech.
- Late August: PCE inflation data, plus 2-, 5- and 7-year Treasury auctions.
- Throughout: oil prices and news on the Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz, Treasury's refunding and buyback plans, and how much markets price a September 15 to 16 rate hike.

**Bottom line:** The 10-year was at about 4.70% to 4.75% at the start of August, its highest since January 2025. The main drivers are oil prices and the chance of a Fed hike.
